title: A Sky Primitive is a standardized interface through which Agents leverage Sky Protocol's permissioned infrastructure
content:
A.2.2 defines a Sky Primitive as "a standardized interface that allows Agents to connect to, and leverage, Sky Protocol's permissioned infrastructure," and states that the Article "defines each of the Sky Primitives available for Prime Agents to use to expand the Sky Ecosystem."

Two words carry the weight. **Permissioned**: Primitives are the gate through which Agents reach protocol capabilities they cannot otherwise touch, so the set of Primitives is exactly the set of things an Agent is allowed to do with Sky's infrastructure. **Standardized**: A.2.2.1.4.2 confirms that "every Primitive instance abides by a standardized data model specified at the Sky Core level, ensuring that all Prime Agents, Executor Agents and other actors are able to submit and track the necessary data reliably."

The consequence is stated directly: "Each Prime Agent strategy is unique, so each may combine the Sky Primitives differently." Differentiation between Agents is therefore *combinatorial* rather than *architectural* — Agents do not build bespoke connections to the protocol, they select and configure from a shared vocabulary.

This is what makes cross-Agent interoperability and uniform oversight possible at all. It also caps innovation at the boundary of the Primitive set: an Agent whose strategy needs a capability no Primitive exposes cannot simply build it, it must get the Primitive list amended.
description: Standardization is what makes Agent strategy composable: every Prime Agent draws on the same fixed menu of Primitives, and differentiates by how it combines them.
